new.analysis:
The week of Sep 7 – 13 was clean. Every run stayed at 0 of 10 pain, your heart rate stayed in the easy range, and the shin was quiet, so one small step is justified.

Tempo logs each session as one 15 minute run, so I cannot see your run and walk blocks. Three sessions of exactly 15 minutes suggest 5 rounds of 2 minutes running and 1 minute walking, and I have planned from that. If your blocks were different, tell me in your next check-in and I will adjust.

Stress reactions respond badly to a fast rise in load, so the total stays close to last week and only the longest running block grows. The change is small enough that a single bad session would show clearly.

| Measure | Week of Sep 7 – 13 | Week of Sep 14 – 20 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Running minutes (run blocks only) | 30 | 32 |
| Total session time | 45 min | 46 min |
| Longest continuous run block | 2 min | 3 min (Wednesday only) |

The pain rules still apply. Stop any run if the shin aches, as your physio asked. Pain above 3 of 10 during a run, or pain that is worse the next morning, means repeating the last session instead of adding to it. Pain at 3 of 10 or below that settles by the next morning allows the next small step.

Your two rehab sessions and the rest days stay in the week as they are. The rest days give the shin time to settle between runs, and the calf and hip work supports the shin load. Week of Sep 7 – 13 counts as your first of four pain-free weeks, which is the gate before any intervals, hills or strides.
